B1_state_level_counterexamples.name: committed orders cannot be re-planned
B1_state_level_counterexamples.invariant: a customer with a live committed_next never appears in mask / pool_B / any installed plan
B1_state_level_counterexamples.construction: pick a decision point where some vehicle has status=='committed' and committed_next==c; put c into the mask and into a candidate plan
B1_state_level_counterexamples.expected_before_assembly: decision_pool_from_vehicles excludes c and validate_mask_scope raises AssertionError, BUT d3_geo_adapter has no committed check of its own (plan-level API) -- so an assembly that forgets the scope assertion can re-plan c
B1_state_level_counterexamples.why_fakes_insufficient: requires real VehicleState.status/committed_next plus the real pool functions

B1_state_level_counterexamples.name: served (executed prefix) customers cannot enter a plan
B1_state_level_counterexamples.invariant: no served customer appears in any plan suffix or defer set
B1_state_level_counterexamples.construction: pick a decision point with served_route non-empty / served_mask true; insert a served customer into the candidate plan
B1_state_level_counterexamples.expected_before_assembly: validate_full_partition(served_mask=...) reports served_planned -> ok=False, but _commit performs NO validation and would commit it if it were the head
B1_state_level_counterexamples.why_fakes_insufficient: needs a real served_mask and a real commit loop

B1_state_level_counterexamples.name: protected (reserved) vehicles are untouched
B1_state_level_counterexamples.invariant: protected vehicle plans are byte-identical before and after the repair
B1_state_level_counterexamples.construction: designate protected = {reserved vehicle ids}; put a protected-tail customer into the mask
B1_state_level_counterexamples.expected_before_assembly: mask_candidate_pool(protected=...) excludes it and validate_repair_plan reports protected_vehicle_changed
B1_state_level_counterexamples.why_fakes_insufficient: protected semantics interact with the real plan suffixes and get_reserved_customers

B1_state_level_counterexamples.name: STATE VERSION CHANGE after certification
B1_state_level_counterexamples.invariant: a plan certified at event k must not be installed if the state has moved on
B1_state_level_counterexamples.construction: certify plan P at event k (record state_hash); advance to event k+1 where a reveal fires (strict_online_env.py:528 clears every non-closed vehicle's mutable_suffix and sets needs_replan) or where clock/ready_time advance; then attempt the install
B1_state_level_counterexamples.expected_before_assembly: NOTHING checks this: there is no live-path state identity at all (env.snapshot_hook defaults to None) and the plan carries no clock/version/state field
B1_state_level_counterexamples.why_fakes_insufficient: this is precisely a property of the real event loop; a synthetic clock bump on a plan dict proves nothing
B1_state_level_counterexamples.note: this counterexample CANNOT EVEN BE EXPRESSED before the assembly makes the state identity computable -- that is the first B2 work item

B1_state_level_counterexamples.name: post-certification commit failure / install-CALLED but not-committed
B1_state_level_counterexamples.invariant: callback_invoked must never be reported as a successful commit; an illegal head must not be committed
B1_state_level_counterexamples.construction: certify successfully, then make the head illegal (head customer already served / vehicle status became closed / ready_time advanced) and run the commit loop; alternatively write the suffix so the head lands on a vehicle that the loop skips
B1_state_level_counterexamples.expected_before_assembly: _commit performs ZERO feasibility checks (it computes arrive/finish and writes committed_next unconditionally), and the loop at strict_online_env.py:650-655 only pops for status in (idle, ready) -- so a closed vehicle is silently skipped with no record
B1_state_level_counterexamples.why_fakes_insufficient: the whole point is the interaction between the replanner write-back and the env commit loop

B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.name: state drift with an unchanged plan must be refused
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.construction: certify at event k; advance clock / fire a reveal without changing the plan suffix; then install
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.expected_before_assembly: no live-path state identity exists -> not expressible

B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.name: contract drift with an unchanged plan must be refused
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.invariant: install requires contract_hash / effective_contract_hash / profile_hash unchanged
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.construction: certify under ColdChainContract v1; swap in a ColdChainContractV2 (or apply a different ObjectiveProfile) in-process; install the same plan
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.expected_before_assembly: the install gate compares plan hashes only; it never reads the contract
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.constraint: ColdChainContractV2 has NO from_manifest / loader (whole-tree search) -> the counterexample must build the v2 contract in-process

B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.name: capture-anchor ambiguity (not a defect, a declaration requirement)
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.invariant: the credential must declare whether state identity is pre-prepare or post-prepare
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.construction: capture state identity at the same decision point both before and after prepare_decision_point (which mutates ready_time)
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.expected: the two hashes necessarily differ; the purpose is to force an explicit state_capture_anchor field rather than an implicit one

B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.name: plan-hash blind spot: same plan hash, different anchor
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.invariant: the credential must be sensitive to anchor_time / anchor_load changes
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.construction: build two plans with identical (vehicle key, anchor_node, suffix) but different anchor_time (equivalently: a state change that moved ready_time / committed_finish without changing the suffix)
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.expected_before_assembly: plan_hash returns the SAME 16-hex value for both, so the existing gate PASSES -- proving 'binding plan_hash alone' is insufficient by construction, not merely in theory
B2_triple_identity_counterexamples.remediation: record plan_hash_strong (a digest covering anchor_time/anchor_load) + explicit anchor_fields; replacing the gate's judgement is a SEMANTIC CHANGE needing its own contract test

independent_reload_definition: recompute state_hash and plan_hash in-process from the receipt and get equality
reproduce P_after_install deterministically from P_certified + the commit rule
head_committed records agree with the live VehicleState
an independent reviewer can decide 'was it really committed' without trusting any boolean flag
explicit_non_claims: no durable/on-disk persistence exists today (G0-Safety batch 1 receipts are in-memory only; asserted still absent by the Green Phase block R1)
state-level rollback is NOT implementable today: no replanner keeps a pre/post STATE pair; only plan-level rollback plus state-identity refusal
cross-process state_hash recomputation is an OPEN decision (JSON round-trip does not reproduce it)
known_gaps_to_close: JF1HRepairReplanner.export_state() carries only {version, baseline, slack_vehicles, deferred_customers, status_inst}; FeatureLocalReplanner does not override it, so decision_log / event_plans / _accepts_total do not enter a snapshot
P_before / P_after are logged on the ACCEPT path only (feature_local_replanner.py:419-422); reject paths (371-373, 398-401) omit them
InstallLedger stores plan value copies, not vehicle/env state

open_design_questions_for_the_user: R1 state identity anchor: post-prepare (recommended) vs pre-prepare
R2 authoritative lock semantics: mask_candidate_pool (recommended) vs get_reserved_customers, and record the difference set
R3 whether the composed certifier should be lifted out of run_exp_energy_c0.py into simulation/ (a source-identity change) or imported as-is (recommended)
R4 cross-process state_hash reproducibility: constrain the receipt to in-process recomputation, or define a new reproducible on-disk serialization as its own work item
R5 where to put the pre-commit re-validation (wrap _plan_and_commit) given _commit itself never validates
R7 plan-identity strengthening: add plan_hash_strong + anchor fields, and accept that changing the gate's judgement is a semantic change requiring its own contract test
